neighbours.label: weak pole on word-final suffix pieces that complete a long or rare word split into pieces (sea·h·orse, unshak·able, harass·ment, erad·ication); no single token
fire: The diver photographed a tiny seahorse clinging to the weed.
Her faith in the plan was unshakable from the first day.
The school has a strict policy against harassment of any kind.
A pregnant male seahorse carries the eggs in a pouch.
He spoke with unshakable confidence about the result.
The union filed a complaint about harassment by a supervisor.
The children drew a seahorse and a starfish on the wall.
They shared an unshakable belief that the river would rise.
quiet: The diver photographed a tiny crab hiding in the weed.
Her faith in the plan was strong from the first day.
The school has a strict policy against bullying of any kind.
A male penguin carries the egg on his feet.
He spoke with great confidence about the result.
The union filed a complaint about abuse by a supervisor.
The children drew a horse and a star on the wall.
They shared a firm belief that the river would rise.

short: suffix piece of a split word
notes: Card: max only 0.64 with one outlier ('top' in Galaktophagoi); the rest of the top examples are 0.32–0.42 on suffix pieces (orse, iers, ting, plies, ment, ization, able, ication). Probes: seahorse 0.46, unshakable 0.52, Harassment 0.26, eradication 0.10, plain sentence 0.03. Tokenisation of the test words was not checked, so some fire items may not split as hoped.
